topic.title: IBM/BeeAI Agent Communication Protocol — history and A2A migration

outcomes: Explain original IBM/BeeAI ACP REST/HTTP, synchronous/asynchronous and SSE design.
Describe current status: IBM Research says ACP is now part of A2A under the Linux Foundation.
Distinguish IBM Agent Communication Protocol from IDE Agent Client Protocol.
Map legacy discovery, run/session IDs, messages, multimodal payloads and streaming events to A2A concepts without assuming one-to-one equivalence.
Design a staged migration with adapters, parity tests, security parity, telemetry, canary and rollback.
prerequisites: Stage 7 Topics 1–6: MCP, A2A Agent Cards, tasks, artifacts and trust boundaries
HTTP/REST, SSE, JSON, OAuth and API migration fundamentals

glossary.definition: An earlier IBM/BeeAI protocol for agent-to-agent communication using HTTP/REST, sync/async interactions, multimodal messages and SSE.
A different protocol for IDE/client-to-coding-agent communication; not IBM/BeeAI ACP.
A boundary translating legacy requests and responses into a target protocol while preserving semantics.
A legacy identifier for one ACP execution; may map to A2A task ID after lifecycle review.
A legacy conversation identifier; may map to A2A context ID after ownership and expiry review.
A transformation preserving meaning, authorization, lifecycle and error behavior—not just field names.
A staged replacement moving traffic to a target while retaining a temporary rollback path.
A test proving migrated behavior and security match required legacy guarantees.

explanation.problem: Protocol names and project status can become stale. IBM/BeeAI's Agent Communication Protocol was introduced for agent interoperability over HTTP. IBM Research now explicitly states that ACP is part of A2A under the Linux Foundation. Understand the original design for existing systems, but avoid starting a new standalone IBM ACP deployment when the intended direction is A2A.
explanation.plainLanguage:
First disambiguate the acronym. This lesson covers IBM/BeeAI Agent Communication Protocol. It is not the Agent Client Protocol used by IDEs and coding-agent clients.

The original IBM ACP focused on agent-to-agent communication. IBM described a REST-based HTTP interface, optional SDKs, multimodal messages, synchronous and asynchronous execution, Server-Sent Events (SSE) for streaming, and metadata-based discovery. BeeAI provided an implementation ecosystem. Agents built with different frameworks could interoperate without exposing internal models, prompts or tools.

The current-status update from IBM Research is decisive: ACP is now part of A2A under the Linux Foundation. Treat IBM ACP as historical protocol knowledge and migration context. For new interoperable agent systems, use the released A2A specification and supported SDKs. Pin the protocol version; this lesson uses A2A 1.0.0 as its released baseline and does not silently mix development-branch changes.

Migration is not a blind endpoint rename. Inventory every legacy endpoint, request/response schema, session/run identifier, event type, content part, authentication method, timeout, retry and error. A legacy synchronous response may map to an immediate A2A Message. A long-running run may map to an A2A Task. A session identifier may map to contextId only if ownership, lifecycle and retention semantics align. Legacy SSE events may map to A2A task status and artifact update events, but event ordering, chunk assembly and reconnect behavior must be tested.

Discovery also changes. Legacy metadata or registry records do not automatically become valid Agent Cards. Publish a trusted Agent Card with supported interfaces, protocol version, skills, capabilities, modalities and security schemes. Validate origin and supported binding before sharing private task context. A card advertises capabilities; authentication and authorization still happen separately.

Multimodal payloads need deliberate mapping. Text, image, file, embedding or structured data may map to A2A Message Parts or Artifact Parts. Validate MIME type, size, encoding, external URL allow-list, provenance and access control. Never treat a legacy opaque payload as trusted instructions.

A safe migration uses a compatibility adapter. It accepts the old contract at the edge, validates identity and tenant, translates into A2A messages/tasks, records an idempotency key and maps A2A results back only for consumers that still need the legacy response. Keep domain policy, tool authorization, approval and business state outside the adapter. Run parity tests and read-only shadow comparisons before moving traffic. Use canary routing, metrics and rollback. Remove the old endpoint only after clients migrate and audit evidence confirms cutover.

ACP and MCP are complementary but distinct. MCP connects an agent to tools, resources and prompts. A2A connects one agent to another. A migrated A2A specialist may still use MCP internally for its own data and tool access.
explanation.mentalModel: Identify legacy ACP scope → inventory wire and lifecycle semantics → map to A2A 1.0.0 → translate through a secure adapter → prove parity → canary → cut over → retire legacy path.
limitations: IBM Research's current status notice is authoritative for project direction; check current A2A specification and releases before migration.
A2A and IBM ACP are not field-for-field identical; preserve semantics with explicit mapping and tests.
Run/session IDs may have different lifecycle, ownership and retention semantics from taskId/contextId.
Legacy event streams may not map directly to A2A status/artifact events; chunk ordering and resume must be tested.
A compatibility adapter can become permanent technical debt; define owner and retirement date.
This is not the IDE Agent Client Protocol; do not reuse its messages or session model.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A company replaces an old ticketing API with a new standard. The adapter translates old ticket requests to new tasks while keeping permissions and status meaning intact. Renaming ticketId to taskId is not enough; preserve ownership, statuses and attachment delivery.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: Suppose the old service has 10,000 weekly runs: 8,000 synchronous and 2,000 asynchronous. A 5% canary routes 500 runs to the A2A adapter. If 498 return equivalent outcomes, parity is 99.6%. One cross-tenant disclosure is still a hard stop even with 99.6% parity.
explanation.productionImpact: Production migration needs a protocol-version matrix, semantic mapping document, compatibility adapter, idempotency, dual-run policy, trace correlation, tenant/auth parity, payload limits, event ordering, SSE reconnect strategy, canary thresholds, rollback switch and explicit legacy retirement criteria.

useCase.scenario: A BeeAI-based service still exposes a legacy IBM ACP-compatible agent endpoint. An organization migrates its orchestrator to A2A 1.0.0 while temporarily preserving the old client contract through an adapter.
inputs: Legacy REST run request and session metadata
A2A Agent Card and supported interface
constraints: Never trust tenant identity from payload alone.
Do not duplicate a side effect during dual-run or retry.
Translate synchronous and asynchronous outcomes according to explicit policy.
Preserve artifact provenance and event ordering.
Legacy endpoint remains available only during approved migration window.
useCase.successMetric: Legacy consumers receive equivalent outcomes while new execution uses A2A, with zero cross-tenant leaks and no duplicate side effects.

dataFlow.purpose: Accept old contract during migration window.
Derive trusted identity and enforce policy.
Validate A2A 1.0.0 interface and security scheme.
Map progress and outputs to legacy consumers.
Record parity, retries and migration evidence.

trustBoundaries: Legacy request body never supplies trusted tenant or role claims.
Adapter can call only the A2A client and application-owned gateway.
Agent Card and remote artifacts are untrusted until origin/schema/provenance validation.
Dual-run never duplicates write-side effects; shadow mode uses read-only or simulated execution.
Correlation IDs are opaque and do not grant task access.
failurePaths: Unknown legacy field: reject or quarantine; do not silently drop security-relevant data.
No semantic mapping for a status: fail closed and alert migration owner.
A2A Agent Card version mismatch: route to legacy only if rollback policy explicitly permits it.
Duplicate legacy request: return prior task mapping using idempotency key.
A2A task times out: preserve unknown/in-progress state and reconcile before retry.
Artifact translation loses MIME/provenance: quarantine and block consumer delivery.
Canary parity or safety threshold fails: stop rollout and revert routing switch.

stages.title: Inventory legacy contract
stages.narration: Capture the legacy REST endpoint, session/run IDs, payload types, SSE events and auth behavior.
stages.transformation: record schema, lifecycle, scopes, retries and error codes

stages.title: Map semantics
stages.narration: Map legacy session to context and run to task only after ownership and lifecycle review.

stages.title: Translate through adapter
stages.narration: Adapter validates tenant and idempotency before sending an A2A message.

stages.title: Prove parity
stages.narration: Compare final result, event order, artifacts, approval and authorization against legacy expectations.

stages.title: Canary and retire
stages.narration: Move a small percentage of traffic, monitor rollback thresholds and retire old route after clients migrate.

controls.name: canary_percent
controls.effect: Percentage of new requests routed through the A2A adapter.

controls.name: parity_rate
controls.effect: Behavioral parity rate; low parity blocks promotion.

controls.name: critical_security_failures
controls.effect: Any critical security failure blocks rollout regardless of parity.

controls.name: duplicate_side_effects
controls.effect: Any duplicate write-side effect blocks rollout.

steps.reasoning: Record request schema, identity source, session/run semantics, SSE ordering and error behavior.
Map session to contextId and run to taskId only after verifying ownership and retention behavior.
Adapter sends A2A message with a stable idempotency key and minimum necessary context.
Compare translated task state, artifacts and approval requirement against legacy golden trace.

workedExample.expectedOutput: A traceable migration with equivalent business outcome, one logical execution, preserved artifact provenance and a rollback path.

SQLite migration ledger with immutable mapping versions, idempotency, parity records, canary gates and rollback state.

failures.name: Acronym collision
failures.symptom: An IDE Agent Client Protocol integration is mistakenly migrated as IBM ACP.
failures.rootCause: The same acronym is used for different protocol scopes.
failures.recovery: Use full protocol names in packages, docs, service names and architecture records.
failures.regressionTest: Architecture contract explicitly labels IBM/BeeAI ACP vs Agent Client Protocol.

failures.name: Blind field rename
failures.symptom: Old session/run fields are renamed but task ownership or retention semantics change.
failures.recovery: Write semantic mapping and validate context/task ownership, TTL and lifecycle.
failures.regressionTest: Cross-tenant and wrong-context migration cases fail closed.

failures.name: Event loss or reorder
failures.symptom: Legacy SSE consumers miss artifact chunks or see final state before progress.
failures.rootCause: No event sequence/cursor mapping and reconnect policy.
failures.recovery: Persist event sequence and map status/artifact events with replay protection.
failures.regressionTest: Disconnect/reconnect and verify ordered, non-duplicated consumer view.

failures.name: Duplicate side effect during dual-run
failures.symptom: Legacy and A2A paths both execute the same refund.
failures.rootCause: Shadow comparison runs write-capable paths twice.
failures.recovery: Use read-only shadow mode, stable idempotency key and one authoritative writer.
failures.regressionTest: Repeated request and dual-run create one logical operation.

failures.name: Security parity regression
failures.symptom: Migrated endpoint accepts weaker scopes or leaks another tenant's artifacts.
failures.rootCause: Authentication and authorization were treated as transport details.
failures.recovery: Preserve identity, scopes, tenant binding and artifact ACLs as hard gates.
failures.regressionTest: Cross-tenant access and missing scope block canary.

miniAppIntegration.projectGoal: Build a migration workbench that compares legacy ACP contracts with A2A target semantics and gates rollout.
steps: Identify whether the source protocol is IBM/BeeAI ACP or Agent Client Protocol.
Load legacy endpoint, schema, event and security inventory.
Map sync response to Message and long-running run to Task where semantics permit.
Map session/run IDs to contextId/taskId and validate tenant ownership.
Translate SSE progress/artifact events and test reconnect ordering.
Run parity and adversarial security cases; reject critical failures.
Enable read-only shadow and small canary; verify rollback before promotion.
Track old-client usage and retire the legacy endpoint only after migration evidence is complete.

scenarioQuiz.question: What is the current status of IBM/BeeAI Agent Communication Protocol according to IBM Research?
options: It is the same as IDE Agent Client Protocol
It is now part of A2A under the Linux Foundation
scenarioQuiz.explanation: IBM Research explicitly says ACP is now part of A2A under the Linux Foundation.

scenarioQuiz.question: Can a legacy session ID always be renamed to contextId?
options: Yes, fields with similar names are equivalent
No, validate ownership, lifecycle, retention and conversation semantics
Only if it is a UUID
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Migration is semantic; an ID mapping must preserve meaning and authorization.

scenarioQuiz.question: How should dual-run compare old and new implementations?
options: Use read-only shadow or one authoritative writer with shared idempotency
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Shadow comparisons must not duplicate side effects.

scenarioQuiz.question: What is a valid rollout gate?
options: High average parity even with one tenant leak
No critical security failures and no duplicate side effects
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Critical security and side-effect correctness are non-compensable gates.

rubric.evidence: Distinguish IBM/BeeAI ACP from Agent Client Protocol and state the current A2A direction.
Map run/session/message/event/artifact concepts with documented compatibility rules.
Preserve trusted identity, tenant scope, authorization and artifact ACLs.
Build adapter, parity tests, idempotency, shadow, canary and rollback.
Define consumer telemetry, deprecation notice and legacy shutdown criteria.

evidence: Legacy contract and mapping matrix are versioned.
No duplicate side effects occur during retries or shadow runs.
Parity tests include events, artifacts and security cases.
Canary can be rolled back and retirement is evidence based.

codeWalkthrough.lines: legacy session_id → contextId only after semantic review
codeWalkthrough.explanation: Conversation grouping, retention and ownership must match; a field rename is not enough.

codeWalkthrough.lines: legacy run_id → taskId with idempotency key
codeWalkthrough.explanation: One legacy execution should map to one logical target task across retries.

codeWalkthrough.lines: legacy SSE event → statusUpdate or artifactUpdate
codeWalkthrough.explanation: Preserve event order, cursor, artifact identity and replay semantics.
A good aggregate parity score cannot compensate for a critical security regression.
Traffic movement is controlled by evidence and a tested rollback path, not a calendar date.
